incidents.vector: Single operator across three npm aliases (mr.4nd3r50n, ce-rwb, t-in-one) published 43 malicious packages impersonating internal corporate namespaces across nine organizational scopes including Sberbank's SberPay widget, using dependency confusion and obfuscated postinstall reconnaissance payloads.
incidents.impact: Packages run silently during npm install, fingerprint developer environments, and exfiltrate hostnames, env vars and credentials to attacker-controlled C2 with a RECON_ONLY flag designed for staged follow-on exploitation. Microsoft and npm removed the packages and maintainer accounts.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters-linked actors phished a single employee account in April 2026, gained access to a portion of Carnival's IT environment, and copied personal data including passport and driver's license numbers.
incidents.impact: Carnival confirmed on May 28 that records of approximately 6 million customers (per Maine AG filing) were exposed; attackers earlier dumped what they claimed were 8.7 million records, including data tied to Holland America's Mariner Society loyalty program.

incidents.victim: Cloud and CI/CD developer environments (OpenSearch/Elastic ecosystem)
incidents.vector: Maintainer vpmdhaj published 14 typosquat npm packages spoofing OpenSearch/Elastic libraries; preinstall hooks downloaded a Bun-compiled stage-2 payload that harvested AWS IMDSv2/ECS credentials, HashiCorp Vault tokens, npm publish tokens and GitHub Actions secrets.
incidents.impact: Stolen npm publish tokens enable further downstream supply-chain pivoting; AWS STS sessions and Secrets Manager material were exfiltrated from affected runners. Microsoft and npm removed the packages and Defender now blocks the binaries.

incidents.vector: Hacker exploited an unpatched vulnerability in March 2026 to enter Ajax's systems multiple times; Dutch police arrested a 35-year-old suspect in Buren on May 27 and seized digital storage devices.
incidents.impact: Ajax originally disclosed exposure of several hundred email addresses; Dutch broadcaster RTL reported the breach may have exposed personal information of more than 300,000 registered supporters and affected 42,000 season tickets, with the attacker also able to transfer tickets and alter stadium-ban records.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupted email servers for the U.S. territory's government; officials did not confirm whether the incident was ransomware.
incidents.impact: Administrative tasks across the territorial government were slowed as the email system was taken offline. Investigation ongoing.

incidents.victim: German university hospitals (Cologne, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Ulm, Mannheim)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Unimed, a third-party billing service provider for privately insured and self-paying patients, in mid-April 2026 and stole patient data from its systems.
incidents.impact: Confirmed exposure of patient information across at least six university hospitals — including roughly 30,000 at Cologne, 54,000 at Freiburg, 11,000 at Heidelberg, and 1,600 at Ulm — with smaller subsets exposing diagnosis, treatment and bank/payment data. No attacker has claimed responsibility; hospitals filed criminal complaints.

incidents.victim: U.S., Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern technology sector targets
incidents.vector: Screening Serpens (Iran-nexus APT, also tracked as UNC1549/Smoke Sandstorm) used tailored recruitment-themed spear phishing impersonating a global air carrier and a popular video conferencing platform; archives with fake job PDFs side-loaded six new RAT variants (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2) via AppDomainManager hijacking.
incidents.impact: Campaigns ran mid-February through April 2026 in step with the regional conflict that began Feb 28; samples surfaced from victims in the U.S., Israel and the UAE plus two additional Middle Eastern entities. Each variant routed C2 through 3–5 unique Azure-hosted domains for resilience.

incidents.vector: Attackers used compromised credentials issued to other authorized government agencies to access the state registry's land and real-estate database.
incidents.impact: 600,000 records exfiltrated, including real names, cadastral data and other real-estate-specific details. Lithuanian authorities are investigating.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters listed Charter on its dark-web leak portal; Charter has confirmed the incident but has not yet detailed the intrusion method.
incidents.impact: Scope of stolen data not yet publicly disclosed; the listing is consistent with ShinyHunters' ongoing campaign of high-volume data theft and extortion against large U.S. enterprises.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to NYC Health + Hospitals systems and exfiltrated highly sensitive medical and biometric records.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected. Stolen data includes medical information plus fingerprints and palm prints — biometric data that cannot be changed or replaced for affected individuals.

incidents.vector: Play ransomware group claimed to have breached MyPillow's corporate network and exfiltrated sensitive financial documents prior to extortion.
incidents.impact: Play has begun extortion based on the claimed data theft; MyPillow has not publicly confirmed the incident. Damage and final ransom demand not yet disclosed.

incidents.vector: An Elasticsearch database was left unprotected on the open internet for at least two months before being secured.
incidents.impact: Personal details of nearly 19 million customers exposed, including phone numbers and full names tied to WeChat accounts. No confirmation that data was exfiltrated by malicious actors before secure-down.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf IoT-botnet victims (incl. U.S. Department of Defense address ranges)
incidents.vector: Operator known as 'Dort' built and rented the Kimwolf IoT botnet — primarily compromised digital photo frames and web cameras — which issued more than 25,000 attack commands at peaks near 30 Tbps, the largest DDoS volumes on record.
incidents.impact: Some victims' losses exceeded $1 million; attacks affected DoD IP ranges. Canadian Ontario Provincial Police arrested Jacob Butler, 23, of Ottawa on a U.S. extradition warrant; U.S. charges carry up to 10 years in prison.

incidents.vector: Criminal group TeamPCP used OIDC credentials harvested in the May 11 TanStack worm to publish a trojanized v18.95.0 of the Nx Console VS Code extension under the verified nrwl.angular-console publisher; the extension was live for ~18 minutes and auto-updated on a GitHub employee endpoint, enabling lateral movement through internal CI/CD.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories exfiltrated and offered for sale on a cybercrime forum for $50,000. OpenAI, Grafana Labs and Mistral AI were named downstream victims. GitHub rotated critical secrets the same day; ~61,274 npm granular access tokens with write/2FA-bypass permissions were invalidated.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Azure Durable Functions SDK users (durabletask PyPI package)
incidents.vector: Three malicious versions (1.4.1–1.4.3) of Microsoft's officially published durabletask Python SDK were uploaded to PyPI within a ~35-minute window with a dropper injected directly into the package source files, making import alone sufficient to trigger execution.
incidents.impact: Second-stage payload steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp Vault, 1Password and Bitwarden, and propagates inside cloud environments via AWS SSM and 'kubectl exec'; independent reporting characterises the stage-2 payload as carrying a Linux disk wiper. Versions were yanked within hours; any environment that pulled them is treated as exposed.

incidents.vector: TeamPCP used a compromised 'atool' maintainer account to publish a third Mini Shai-Hulud wave: 639 malicious package versions across 323 packages in a single burst, including 42 packages displaying forged Sigstore verification badges in the npm UI.
incidents.impact: Obfuscated payload ran during npm install on packages including echarts-for-react (~1.1M weekly downloads) and size-sensor (~4.2M weekly downloads), harvesting 20+ credential classes — GitHub/npm tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes accounts, Vault and Stripe secrets — and persisting via .vscode/tasks.json and ~/.claude/settings.json.

incidents.vector: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit unsealed a U.S. District Court action and seized Fox Tempest infrastructure, taking hundreds of Azure VMs offline and revoking over 1,000 fraudulent Microsoft Artifact Signing certificates used to legitimise malware.
incidents.impact: Service had operated since May 2025 and was used by ransomware affiliates of Rhysida, INC, Qilin and Akira to sign Oyster, Lumma Stealer and Vidar payloads masquerading as AnyDesk, Teams, PuTTY and Webex. Microsoft analysed millions of dollars in cryptocurrency payments tied to the operation; attacks targeted organisations in the U.S., China, France and India.

incidents.victim: WorkTitans BV / MIRhosting (Stark Industries successor infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Dutch FIOD (financial-crime agency) arrested Andrey Nesterenko (39) and Youssef Zinad (57) for violating EU sanctions; they ran the.hosting/WorkTitans and MIRhosting networks, which inherited Stark Industries' infrastructure used by Russian intelligence-linked groups.
incidents.impact: More than 800 servers seized across two Dutch data centres, three offices searched, and customer data on seized hardware reported lost. De Volkskrant reporting indicates these networks were the most-used in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during the November 2025 Danish municipal elections.

incidents.vector: Over 5,700 malicious commits pushed to victim repositories on May 18 injected GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate credentials, keys, tokens and other secrets during normal CI runs.
incidents.impact: More than 5,500 GitHub repositories confirmed infected; secrets harvested from CI/CD pipelines enable downstream credential abuse and further supply-chain pivots. Cleanup and credential rotation ongoing across affected organisations.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor with administrative access to the agency's code platform created a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub profile that included plaintext AWS GovCloud keys and credentials to dozens of internal CISA systems, after disabling GitHub's built-in secret-publishing protection.
incidents.impact: 844 MB of sensitive data including AWS GovCloud credentials and RSA private keys granting full access to CISA-IT's GitHub organisation were exposed for months. CISA is still rotating affected secrets more than a week after notification; Congress is demanding answers. CISA states 'no indication' sensitive data was compromised.

incidents.victim: Australian independent MP Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: Suspected foreign state actor compromised the WhatsApp account of an Australian MP and three of her staffers as part of a broader campaign targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: Compromise of communications belonging to a sitting Australian federal MP and her office; the incident was first reported in March and surfaced publicly in late May. Attribution remains unconfirmed but is believed to be part of an ongoing Russian operation against allied parliamentarians.

incidents.vector: Reported intrusion into Taiwan's bullet-train operator highlighted gaps in rail-system cybersecurity; specific access vector not disclosed publicly.
incidents.impact: Incident drew attention to systemic cybersecurity weaknesses across rail operators; no public confirmation of operational disruption or ransomware payment. Investigations and hardening efforts ongoing.
